prompt.context_jp: 独り身を貫く建築家・桑野信介にとって、無言で鉄を持ち上げるジムの時間___数少ない安らぎの一つだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 独り身を貫く建築家・桑野信介にとって、無言で鉄を持ち上げるジムの時間___数少ない安らぎの一つだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the narrator's framing of 'gym time' as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is presenting 'gym time' as the topic being characterized — 'as for gym time, it was one of the few moments of solace.' This is classic topic-marking は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as new identifying information (answering 'which was his solace?'), which doesn't match the reflective framing. を doesn't fit a copular predicate.

contrast_examples.jp: ジムの時間は安らぎだ。
contrast_examples.en: As for gym time, it's solace. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: ジムの時間が安らぎだ。
contrast_examples.en: Gym time is (the one that is) his solace. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 渋々足を運んだ病院で桑野を迎えたの___、遠慮という言葉を持たない女医だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 渋々足を運んだ病院で桑野を迎えたの___、遠慮という言葉を持たない女医だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces the identifying new-information subject?

feedback.correct_en: In the cleft pattern '〜のは…だった' (the one who did X was Y), は marks the presupposed clause as topic while the new identity follows. This is the standard structure here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would break the cleft and sound like a direct subject clause. に doesn't fit grammatically.

contrast_examples.jp: 迎えたのは女医だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who greeted him was a female doctor. (cleft)
A female doctor greeted him. (plain subject)

prompt.context_jp: 問診と説教の境目のような口調に、桑野の眉間___さっそく皺が寄る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 問診と説教の境目のような口調に、桑野の眉間___さっそく皺が寄る。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking where the wrinkles appear.

feedback.correct_en: 寄る takes a に-marked destination ('wrinkles gather at his brow'). The は adds a topic/contrastive nuance on the location.
feedback.incorrect_en: がは and をは are not grammatical combinations in Japanese.

prompt.context_jp: 独身主義者の彼にとって「見合い」の二文字___、想像するだけで気分の重くなる符牒だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 独身主義者の彼にとって「見合い」の二文字___、想像するだけで気分の重くなる符牒だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks '見合いの二文字' as the thing being described?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence defines what 'omiai' means to him — a topic-comment structure. は sets up 'omiai' as the theme to be characterized.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new/identifying info ('it's omiai that is...'), which doesn't match this descriptive framing of a known word.

contrast_examples.en: It's omiai that is the unpleasant word. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 自分で相手を見つけられないから お父さん___心配してるんですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分で相手を見つけられないから お父さん___心配してるんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle explains WHY the father is worried (new info giving the reason)?

feedback.correct_en: In a 'から + reason' subordinate clause introducing why something happens, が marks the subject as newly presented information within that causal clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'お父さん' a topic separate from the reason, weakening the causal link. The doctor is reporting new facts about what is happening.

contrast_examples.jp: お父さんが心配してる。
お父さんは心配してる。

prompt.context_jp: あの人___ ああいう人なの ただ それだけ
prompt.prompt_jp: あの人___ ああいう人なの ただ それだけ
prompt.prompt_en: Natsumi dismisses gossip by setting Kuwano apart. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: は marks Kuwano as the topic being characterized ('that person — he's just that kind of person'). It also carries a mild contrastive 'he, unlike others' nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like identifying 'which person' is like that, not describing him. も would mean 'that person too,' changing the meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: あの人はああいう人だ。
contrast_examples.en: That person is just like that. (topic/contrast)

contrast_examples.jp: あの人がああいう人だ。
contrast_examples.en: HE is the one who's like that. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: ちょうどよかった！ お前___電話しようと思ってたんだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: ちょうどよかった！ お前___電話しようと思ってたんだよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the recipient of the phone call?

feedback.correct_en: 電話する takes に to mark the person being called (the goal/recipient of the action).
feedback.incorrect_en: を doesn't mark call recipients in standard usage; が would make お前 the subject doing the calling.

prompt.context_jp: だったら なんで こいつ___いるんだよ？
prompt.prompt_jp: だったら なんで こいつ___いるんだよ？
prompt.prompt_en: Nakagawa demands to know why Kuwano is present. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Existence/presence questions with なんで focus on the newly noticed subject. が marks こいつ as the new, questioned element: 'why is HE here?'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize こいつ and sound like contrastive background, not the pointed demand the context needs.

prompt.context_jp: 今の女の人 誰ですか？ / なんか とってもきれいな女の人___
prompt.prompt_jp: なんか とってもきれいな女の人___いましたよね
prompt.prompt_en: Sawori mentions newly noticing the woman. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The woman is new information just noticed — 'there WAS this beautiful woman.' が marks newly observed existence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the woman is already a known topic, which contradicts 'なんか…' (a sudden observation).

contrast_examples.en: As for beautiful people, (one) was there. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: あの桑野に若い恋人___できたらしい、という奇妙な噂は、居酒屋の一角にまで届いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: あの桑野に若い恋人___できたらしい
prompt.prompt_en: The rumor reports a new development. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: '恋人ができる' (to come to have a girlfriend) introduces the girlfriend as new information appearing in Kuwano's life — classic が of emergence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat '恋人' as a known topic. を doesn't fit the intransitive できる.

contrast_examples.en: A child came about / was conceived.

prompt.context_jp: 何___起こるか 分からない世の中だからね
prompt.prompt_jp: 何___起こるか 分からない世の中だからね
prompt.prompt_en: Within the embedded question 'what might happen,' which particle marks 何?

feedback.correct_en: Interrogative pronouns like 何 in subject position take が, not は. 何 is the unknown subject of 起こる ('what will happen').
feedback.incorrect_en: 何は is ungrammatical as a question subject. 何を would require a transitive verb, but 起こる is intransitive.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女じゃないって誰___言った？
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女じゃないって誰___言った？
prompt.prompt_en: Kuwano challenges with an interrogative subject. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Interrogative subjects (誰, 何, どれ) take が. 'Who said she isn't my girlfriend?' demands identification of a subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰は is ungrammatical as the subject of a wh-question. 誰も would mean 'nobody said,' flipping the meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野さんって 恋愛___ 興味ないんじゃなかったの？
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野さんって 恋愛___ 興味ないんじゃなかったの？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in '〜に興味ない'?

feedback.correct_en: The fixed pattern '〜に興味がある/ない' marks the object of interest with に.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is not used with 興味. が could mark 興味 itself (興味がない) but not 恋愛 as the target.

prompt.context_jp: 実は 桑野さんに 彼女___いたなんて 悔しくないですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 実は 桑野さんに 彼女___いたなんて 悔しくないですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in the surprising revelation?

feedback.correct_en: The revelation presents 彼女 as new information in Kuwano's life — 'he actually HAS a girlfriend.' Existence/possession with new info takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose 彼女 as a known topic, undercutting the surprise. も would mean 'a girlfriend too,' altering meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野___選んだのは、都合よく、しかも波風を立てないような相手だと踏んだからだという。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野___選んだのは、都合のいい相手だと踏んだからだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Yuki actively chose Kuwano. Which particle marks him as direct object?

feedback.correct_en: 選ぶ is transitive — the thing chosen takes を. 'The reason she chose Kuwano...' makes him the direct object.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 桑野 the one doing the choosing, reversing agency. は would topicalize but still needs an object marker contextually.

prompt.context_jp: それに あの人より 桑野さんのほう___見た目いいし
prompt.prompt_jp: あの人より 桑野さんのほう___見た目いいし
prompt.prompt_en: A comparison is being made. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The pattern 'AよりBのほうが〜' uses が to mark the side that wins in the comparison — exhaustive-listing が: 'Kuwano is the one who looks better.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は doesn't fit this comparative construction's standard form; が is required to highlight the preferred option.

contrast_examples.jp: 夏より冬のほうが好き。

prompt.context_jp: 桑野___彼女ができたことぐらいかなぁ
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野___彼女ができたことぐらいかなぁ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'Kuwano' as the person who got a girlfriend?

feedback.correct_en: '〜に〜ができる' uses に to mark the person who comes to have something. 彼女 then takes が as the new thing that appeared.
feedback.incorrect_en: 桑野が would make him the subject of できる (the thing coming into being), which doesn't match — it's the girlfriend that 'came about.'

contrast_examples.en: He had a child (came to have).

prompt.context_jp: 男___ね 女性が どんなに年下でもＯＫなんですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 男___ね 女性が どんなに年下でもＯＫなんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Kuwano makes a sweeping statement about men as a category. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Generic statements about a category ('as for men...') use は to set the topic. Kuwano is contrasting men with women as a group.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce specific men as new info, which doesn't fit a general claim about 'men in general.'

prompt.context_jp: やっぱり私たち 年___離れ過ぎなんじゃない？
prompt.prompt_jp: やっぱり私たち 年___離れ過ぎなんじゃない？
prompt.prompt_en: 'As for us, our AGE is too far apart.' Which particle for 年?

feedback.correct_en: In the 'topic は subject が' double-subject construction, 私たち is topic and 年 is the specific attribute being commented on, marked by が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は on 年 would create two topics awkwardly. を is wrong since 離れる is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: He is tall (his height is high).

prompt.context_jp: 筋肉痛くらいで大げさに、と口を尖らせる彼を、白衣の相手は___諭しつづけた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 白衣の相手は___諭しつづけた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which adverb fits — the doctor lectured him mercilessly?

feedback.correct_en: 容赦なく ('without mercy') matches the earlier description of her as someone with no concept of restraint — she lectures him unsparingly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 遠慮して (holding back) is the opposite. 気の毒に (sympathetically) doesn't match her blunt character.

prompt.context_jp: 健康のために運動してるのに ___じゃないですか
prompt.prompt_jp: 健康のために運動してるのに ___じゃないですか
prompt.prompt_en: The doctor's idiom meaning 'then it's all for nothing/counterproductive'?

choices.text: 箸にも棒にもかからない

feedback.correct_en: 元も子もない means 'losing both the principal and the interest' — i.e., it defeats the whole purpose. Fits exercising for health but harming yourself.
feedback.incorrect_en: 箸にも棒にも… means 'hopeless/beyond help.' 猫の手も… means 'desperately busy.' Neither fits the counterproductive meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 無理したら元も子もない。
contrast_examples.en: If you overdo it, it's all for nothing.

contrast_examples.jp: 忙しくて猫の手も借りたい。
contrast_examples.en: So busy I'd take any help.

prompt.context_jp: 肉体美を___んです
prompt.prompt_jp: 肉体美を___んです
prompt.prompt_en: Kuwano says he is 'pursuing' physical beauty. Which verb?

feedback.correct_en: 追求する means 'to pursue (an ideal/goal)' — the right word for pursuing beauty, truth, or perfection.
feedback.incorrect_en: 追跡 means to chase/track (a target); 追い抜く means to overtake. Neither fits abstract goals.

prompt.context_jp: よりによって桑野さんに 先 ___なんて
prompt.prompt_jp: よりによって桑野さんに 先 ___なんて
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes 'to be beaten to it by Kuwano of all people'?

feedback.correct_en: 先を越される is a set phrase meaning 'to be beaten to the punch/get overtaken.' Perfect for Michiru's frustration at being surpassed.
feedback.incorrect_en: 先を渡される and 先を折られる are not standard expressions in this meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: ライバルに先を越された。
contrast_examples.en: My rival beat me to it.

prompt.context_jp: 今になってビビッたのよ ___！
prompt.prompt_jp: 今になってビビッたのよ ___！
prompt.prompt_en: Yuki curses her ex. Which insult fits?

feedback.correct_en: 根性なし ('spineless/gutless') is the classic insult for someone who chickens out. Matches Yuki calling her ex a coward for backing down.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気合入り would be a compliment (fired up). 遠慮なし describes someone unreserved, not cowardly.

prompt.context_jp: 人が言うことに いちいち ___入れたりしないしね
prompt.prompt_jp: 人が言うことに いちいち ___入れたりしないしね
prompt.prompt_en: Kuwano means young girls don't 'nitpick' everything. Which word?

feedback.correct_en: 茶々を入れる is the set phrase for 'to butt in / heckle / make snide interjections.' Perfect fit for Kuwano's complaint about Natsumi.
feedback.incorrect_en: お茶を入れる means 'to make tea' — literal, not idiomatic. 水を入れる doesn't form this idiom.

contrast_examples.en: To throw cold water on / spoil the mood.

prompt.context_jp: 姪の無邪気な一言が、大人たちの疑いに___ような形で焚きつけた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 姪の一言が、大人たちの疑いに___ような形で焚きつけた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which idiom means 'adding fuel to the fire'?

feedback.correct_en: 火に油を注ぐ literally 'pour oil on fire' = inflame/aggravate a situation. The niece's remark intensified the adults' suspicions.
feedback.incorrect_en: 水を得た魚 means 'in one's element.' 馬の耳に念仏 means 'wasted on someone.' Neither fits intensification.

contrast_examples.jp: それは火に油を注ぐ結果になった。
contrast_examples.en: That ended up adding fuel to the fire.

prompt.context_jp: 取り繕いきれなかった気まずさを___まま、桑野は逃げるように歩き出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 気まずさを___まま、桑野は歩き出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means 'dragging/lingering' (the awkwardness)?

feedback.correct_en: 引きずる means to drag along — used figuratively for lingering emotions you can't shake off. Fits 'carrying the awkwardness.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 引き受ける means to accept a responsibility. 引き返す means to turn back. Neither fits emotional lingering.

prompt.context_jp: The doctor explains that self-actualization can be an internal journey.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for the line about self-actualization completing within oneself?

choices.text: 自己実現っていうのはね、自分の中だけで完結することもあるんですよ
自己実現というのが、自分の中だけで完結もありますね
自己実現は自分の中だけに完結することもあるですよ

feedback.correct_en: Option (a) uses the natural topic-marker pattern 〜っていうのは with the softening ね, and 完結することもある correctly nominalizes the possibility.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) scrambles particles and omits こと. (c) uses 完結することもあるんです form but wrongly has に instead of で and drops ん, making it unnatural.

contrast_examples.jp: 愛っていうのは難しいものですよ。

prompt.context_jp: Kuwano deflects a question about whether Yuki is his girlfriend.
prompt.prompt_en: Which deflection sounds most natural and in-character for Kuwano?

choices.text: 大体、「彼女」の定義って何なんだ？
だいたい彼女の定義は何でしょうか？
彼女を定義って何だよ？

feedback.correct_en: (a) uses the natural pattern 〜って何なんだ？ with 大体 as a rhetorical opener — fits Kuwano's argumentative casual register.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too polite/stiff for the moment. (c) mis-marks 彼女 with を, breaking the grammar of 'definition of X.'

contrast_examples.jp: 友達の定義は何ですか？
contrast_examples.en: What is the definition of a friend?

prompt.context_jp: The doctor comments on how lifestyle changes can affect health.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural?

choices.text: 急に生活環境が変わると体調崩したりしますよね
急に生活環境を変わると体調を崩したりますよね
急に生活環境は変わる時、体調崩れますよね

feedback.correct_en: (a) uses the natural collocation 体調を崩す (with を dropped colloquially) and conditional と for a general tendency.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) wrongly uses 環境を変わる (変わる is intransitive) and the ungrammatical 崩したります. (c) uses the wrong aspect and particle choices.

contrast_examples.en: When I get tired, I get run-down.

prompt.context_jp: The doctor suggests a 45-year-old partner is just right for Kuwano's age.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural?

choices.text: あなたの年で相手が45ってのは、ちょうどいいじゃないですか
あなたの年に相手は45、ちょうどいいじゃないですか
あなたは年に相手が45ってちょうどいいじゃないですか

feedback.correct_en: (a) uses the natural pattern 〜ってのは (colloquial for というのは) to frame the situation, with で marking the age context.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) and (c) mis-use particles (に vs で) and drop the topicalizing ってのは that makes the comment flow naturally.

contrast_examples.jp: この年で結婚ってのは勇気いる。
contrast_examples.en: Getting married at this age takes courage.

contrast_examples.jp: 相手が年上ってのもいい。
contrast_examples.en: Having an older partner is nice too.

prompt.context_jp: The narration describes Kuwano deliberately letting a misunderstanding stand.
prompt.prompt_en: Which narration reads most naturally?

choices.text: 桑野は年下の彼女という誤解を訂正しないようにしむけ、むしろその言葉尻を面白がって弄びはじめた
桑野は年下の彼女と誤解を訂正しないしむけて、むしろ言葉尻が面白がって弄ぶ始めた
桑野が年下の彼女の誤解は訂正しないにしむけ、言葉尻を面白く弄びはじめた

feedback.correct_en: (a) correctly uses 〜という誤解 to form a noun-modifying clause, the auxiliary pattern 〜ないようにしむける, and the adverbial 面白がって.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) drops という and misuses particles on 言葉尻. (c) switches は/が awkwardly and changes 面白がって to the unnatural 面白く in this context.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女だという誤解を解く。
contrast_examples.en: Clear up the misunderstanding that she's his girlfriend.
